newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cool on French Zaire request.
newsitem.headline: EU cool on French Zaire request.

text.p: French pleas to its European Union partners to support sending a security force to Zaire got a cool reception on Thursday, EU diplomats said.
"France asked its European partners if they could support its ideas," one diplomat said. "There was no response, except for a negative one from Britain."

The refusal of Britain, together with France the only permanent European member of the United Nations Security Council, effectively blocked the French move at a Brussels meeting of high-level officials from the 15-nation bloc.
Another proposal, presented at the EU meeting by Belgium, for EU countries to show restraint in delivering arms to the warring parties received a warmer reception, the diplomat said.
But Britain had insisted on the right of Rwanda and Burundi to self-defence, the diplomat said.
France called on the international community on Thursday to consider setting up a "security framework" for Zaire in which it would participate.
Paris said on Wednesday it would ask its European partners to get involved in creating an airlift of humanitarian supplies to Kisangani and eastern Zaire.
The "security framework" would protect delivery of the supplies in areas threatened by the advance of Tutsi-led rebels against government forces.
